headline: Nasdaq slides 1.9% as Meta and chip stocks drop; bitcoin near $81,600
summary: An hour into Thursday's session the Nasdaq is down about 1.9% and the S&P 500 about 1.1%, as Meta (down about 6%) and AMD (down about 6%) lead a sell-off driven by renewed doubts about the payoff from heavy AI spending. Bitcoin is holding near $81,600, down about 2.6% in a day, ether is near $2,400, and total crypto value is down about 4.8% to $2.76 trillion as smaller coins fall harder. The TSX is down about 0.9% as gold drops 2% and banks slip, while U.S. crude is near $99 on Middle East supply fears and the 10-year Treasury yield eases to about 5.03% as investors buy bonds for safety.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: Fear & Greed still reads 68 (Greed), but bitcoin is down about 2.6% and ether about 2.6% on the day, total crypto value is down about 4.8%, and only a handful of coins such as Monero and Lighter are rising.

stocks.label: Risk-off
stocks.why: The Nasdaq is down about 1.9% and the S&P 500 about 1.1% after the open, with Meta, AMD and Amazon down 4–6%, the VIX fear gauge up about 9% to 18.1, and Brent crude near $112.

drivers.title: AI-spending doubts hit Big Tech and chips
drivers.detail: Meta is down about 6% to near $653 even after beating forecasts, as investors weigh its $135–$145 billion spending plan, negative free cash flow and a surprise new non-voting share class; AMD is down about 6%, Nvidia about 3% and Amazon about 4% ahead of its own results next week. A report that Nvidia and Tesla plan to invest in a Samsung supplier revived worries about 'circular' AI deals, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other.

drivers.title: Stablecoin rules finalized
drivers.detail: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a top U.S. bank regulator, finalized reserve, redemption and risk rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027. Crypto stocks rallied on it Wednesday, but Coinbase and Strategy are giving back 3–4% today with bitcoin.

drivers.title: Strong jobs data, high yields
drivers.detail: Weekly U.S. jobless claims fell 6,000 to 194,000, below the 200,000 economists expected and near the lowest in decades, a sign the job market is still tight. The 10-year Treasury yield has eased to about 5.03% from 5.15% as nervous investors buy bonds, but the Fed is expected to hold at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28.

drivers.title: Oil near $100 on Saudi attacks
drivers.detail: U.S. crude is up about 1.9% to roughly $99 a barrel and Brent near $112, its highest since May, after attacks on Saudi airports and an Aramco oil field and a New York Times report that the U.S. and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed Iran strikes after the Nov. 3 midterms. Higher oil feeds inflation fears, while gold is down about 2% to near $4,067, weighing on Canadian miners.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, bonds, crypto

drivers.title: Bitcoin ETF buying is back, but modest
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $1.08 billion over their latest three days, per SoSoValue data cited by CoinDesk, while ether funds have lost more than $1 billion this month. Analysts note flows remain uneven, and past strong rallies came with steadier daily buying of about $200–$300 million.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada expected to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased, and economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28. Hopes for progress in Canada–U.S. trade talks helped the TSX to a four-week high Wednesday.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Down 2.6% in 24h, up 1.5% this week, to about $81,600 (down 5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin climbed to nearly $85,000 late Wednesday, briefly breaking above the $84,000 ceiling that had stopped it on Oct. 13–14, then fell back below $82,000 overnight as Tesla's and Meta's results revived doubts about AI spending; it has held near $81,600 as the Nasdaq fell after the open. The round trip caused about $431 million of liquidations (leveraged bets closed automatically), per CoinGlass. Bitcoin's share of total crypto value is near 60%, its highest since May, as traders shelter in it while smaller coins slide. Spot bitcoin ETFs still took in more than $1 billion over three days.
crypto.meaning: The quick give-back shows buyers aren't yet strong enough to push it out of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. ETF buying of about $1.08 billion over three days helps, but it is below the pace that came with past strong rallies, and some traders warn that a clean break below about $80,000 could open a slide toward $70,000.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$85,000 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: A weak U.S. open for tech, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher yields and oil could push it below the $80,000 floor, with some traders eyeing $75,000–$70,000 if that gives way.
outlook.watch: Whether tech stocks stabilize this afternoon, the $80,000 and $85,000 levels, daily ETF flows, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 2.6% in 24h, up 2.7% this week, to about $2,405 (down 12.5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back overnight and dipped just under $2,400, and it keeps trailing as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network, though the average staking yield slipped to 2.63%.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Continued outflows or a broad risk-off turn could keep it below $2,400 and send it toward the $2,300 area.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, and the ETH/BTC ratio.

crypto.name: Monero
crypto.move: Up 2.6% in 24h and 17.5% this week, to about $617 (up 8% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Monero, a privacy-focused coin that hides who sends what, is one of the few large coins rising today, trading near $617 after briefly touching about $650 overnight. There is no project-specific news behind it: the latest software release on Oct. 16 was routine maintenance. The run started after veteran chart trader Peter Brandt called XMR his favourite large-cap setup, and futures trading volume has outpaced spot (actual coin) trading, a sign that leveraged bets are doing much of the lifting. Futures funding rates (the fee bullish leveraged traders pay to keep bets open) are running near 70% a year, far above other coins, per CoinDesk, which shows how crowded the bullish side is.
crypto.meaning: Rallies driven by borrowed money can reverse quickly if traders are forced to close positions (a liquidation). Monero is also still about 18% below its January record near $799, and an EU anti-money-laundering rule from July 2027 will bar regulated crypto firms from handling privacy coins, which limits where it can trade.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above the old $600 resistance could keep momentum going toward the $700 area and, beyond that, the January high near $799.
outlook.bearCase: A leverage flush could drag it back through $600 toward the $520–$560 zone where it bounced earlier this month.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds $600, futures open interest and funding rates, spot volume versus futures volume, and any exchange delisting news.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 4.0% in 24h, up 15.9% this week, to about $1,248 (down 18% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders are positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) rose about 19–24%, and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Bitwise's Zcash ETF saw small inflows Tuesday after outflows the day before. Today it is down about 4% as open interest falls, a sign some of those leveraged traders are taking profits.
crypto.meaning: Much of this rally is driven by leverage, and data show sellers stayed active during the rise, so swings both ways can be sharp. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour.

outlook.bullCase: Clearing resistance near $1,375 could bring the September high around $1,700 into view as the upgrade nears.
outlook.bearCase: Leveraged longs getting flushed could pull it back to the $1,190–$1,230 support area, and losing $1,180 would erase the breakout.
outlook.watch: $1,375 resistance, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Up 7.5% in 24h and 24.9% this week, to about $3.65 (down 22% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The token of the Lighter derivatives exchange jumped after reports from its Oct. 21 investor call that it plans to apply for a U.S. licence in November and is weighing access through Robinhood's U.S. platform; neither has been confirmed. Renewed attention on its existing Robinhood Wallet partnership and a Delphi Digital research report added interest.
crypto.meaning: The move rests on unconfirmed plans. Only 25% of the 1 billion tokens are circulating, so future supply is a long-term overhang, and the token is still about half its all-time high.

outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.
outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or profit-taking after a 20% day, could send it back toward $3.20, the bottom of today's range.
outlook.watch: Official statements from Lighter, trading volume versus Hyperliquid, and token unlock schedules.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Down 2.7% in 24h, up 10.5% this week, to about $5.02 (up 10% over 30 days)
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. It led the CoinDesk 100 on Wednesday without a single fresh headline, and is giving some of that back today with the wider market.
crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If momentum fades or the proposal stalls, a pullback toward roughly $4.50–$5.00 would be typical after a run this size.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether it can get back above $5.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Down 1.7% in 24h, up 9.2% this week, to about $0.202 (down 5% over 30 days)
crypto.why: ENA led large-cap gainers on Wednesday, then slipped today as DeFi tokens led crypto lower overnight and ENA about 25% below its late-September peak. The earlier rally looked driven by momentum, with the hourly RSI (a gauge of how overstretched a move is) hitting about 73, an overbought reading. A longer-term support is that the last tranche of early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, ending Ethena's monthly investor unlocks.
crypto.meaning: With the investor unlock overhang gone, ENA's supply picture is cleaner, but USDe, the synthetic dollar that drives Ethena's revenue, is far below its 2025 peak. A one-day pop on no clear news can unwind just as fast.

outlook.bullCase: A sustained move above about $0.2165, with USDe supply growing again, could carry ENA toward the mid-$0.20s.
outlook.bearCase: If the overbought bounce fades, a drop under about $0.195 (its 50-day average) would erase this week's gains.
outlook.watch: USDe supply, the $0.195–$0.2165 range, and broader altcoin risk appetite.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Down 2.9% in 24h, up 2.3% this week, to about $1.32 (down 14% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP is drifting lower with the rest of the market after a brief bounce on Wednesday. On the network side, a planned XRP Ledger bug fix was pushed back to November after support from validators (the computers that approve changes) briefly dipped, per a CoinDesk headline. Ripple's push to offer round-the-clock stock trading on crypto rails remains in the news, but no single catalyst explains today's move. CoinDesk notes XRP is trading below its Ichimoku cloud, a chart indicator that some traders read as a sign of building downward momentum.
crypto.meaning: XRP tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions, so it mostly reflects overall risk appetite. The 30-day trend is still down about 14%, and the delayed ledger fix is a minor technical setback rather than a security event.

outlook.bullCase: A broader crypto rally led by bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 could lift XRP back toward the $1.45–$1.50 area.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin breaks below $80,000, XRP would likely lose the $1.30 area and could test about $1.20.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, the rescheduled XRP Ledger fix in November, and U.S. digital-asset rules.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 1.6% in 24h, up 3.3% this week, to about $104.80 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana completed its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality (the point at which a payment can't be reversed), according to CoinDesk. The price has moved roughly in line with the market rather than rallying on the news, slipping about 3% at one point overnight.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch is a meaningful technical milestone, but the market is treating it as already expected. The first days after a big upgrade are when problems usually show up, so stability matters more than headlines.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin break below $80,000, could push SOL under $100.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Down about 6.3% to $653 Thursday morning (low about $648), after closing Wednesday at $697.52
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating forecasts, and fourth-quarter guidance topped estimates, but the stock is falling as investors focus on costs: Meta expects $135–$145 billion of capital spending, free cash flow was about -$2.1 billion this quarter, and a $9.9 billion legal charge cut reported profit. It also surprised Wall Street with a new non-voting Class C share, one for every share held starting in January 2027; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth called the pending shares an overhang (a supply worry hanging over the price) and urged Meta to issue any new stock quickly.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: At least 13 brokerages raised price targets after the results, per LSEG; if buyers return to the strong ad growth, it could recover toward the $700 level.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended AI spending, a share sale to fund it, or the $25 billion New Mexico penalty could push it toward the $620–$630 area.
outlook.watch: Whether $650 holds, any details on Class C share issuance, and Alphabet's and Microsoft's spending plans on Oct. 28.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.move: Down about 6.1% to $519 Thursday morning, about 21% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: There is no AMD-specific news; it is falling in a broad AI-chip sell-off as Meta's spending plans and a report that Nvidia and Tesla will invest $2.8 billion in Samsung Electro-Mechanics revived worries about 'circular' financing, where chip buyers and sellers fund each other. Intel is down about 5% and Nvidia about 3%. AMD also trades at a high valuation, about 200 times its past year's earnings, which leaves little room for disappointment.
stocks.meaning: AMD has been one of the biggest AI winners of the past year, more than doubling from its low, so it swings hard when sentiment turns. Its own results on Nov. 3 are the next real test of whether AI chip demand is holding up.

outlook.bullCase: Strong Microsoft and Alphabet spending plans on Oct. 28 and solid guidance on Nov. 3 could lift it back toward $560–$600.
outlook.bearCase: If the AI-spending worry deepens, it could slide toward the $470–$480 area where it traded in late September.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: About flat at $386 Thursday morning, after dropping to about $374 early on its earnings
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares fell about 5% before the open as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year. Buyers stepped in after the open and erased the early loss.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which explains the early selling.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the early dip resumes and analysts trim targets, it could slide back toward $355–$375.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds today's rebound above $380, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

outlook.bearCase: A credible Iran deal that sends oil sharply lower would hit CNQ, possibly back toward C$70–C$72.

newCoins.name: Pearl
newCoins.what: A Bitcoin-style blockchain launched in April 2026 whose mining is meant to do AI-style math (matrix multiplication) instead of pure puzzle-solving.
newCoins.why: It is trending on CoinGecko and in the top 100 at about $2.19: down about 10% today but up about 20% this week and 113% over 30 days, riding the 'useful AI mining' story.
newCoins.redFlags: A researcher found the main mining software contained no actual AI code, and a co-founder admitted miners can 'spam mine'. Supply grows by about 1 million tokens a day, roughly doubling over the next year. It trades on very few exchanges with thin liquidity.

newCoins.name: Midnight
newCoins.what: A privacy-focused blockchain linked to Cardano; its v8 upgrade lets developers build private smart contracts and tokens.
newCoins.why: NIGHT has rebounded on the upgrade, up about 64% over 30 days to roughly $0.039 and in the top 100, though it is down about 5% today and 6% this week.
newCoins.redFlags: About 515 million NIGHT were stolen in a July bridge hack. Airdrop ('Glacier Drop') claims keep unlocking until early December, which could add selling pressure, and about 7 billion of 24 billion tokens are not yet circulating.

sources.title: CryptoTicker: Midnight NIGHT nearly doubles on v8 upgrade

newCoins.name: Axis Robotics
newCoins.what: A 'physical AI' data project that sold tokens to the public in late September at $0.10 each on the Base network.
newCoins.why: It is trending on CoinGecko at about $0.28, well above its sale price, with a market value near $47 million.
newCoins.redFlags: Very new with little track record. 75% of sale tokens unlock after a six-month cliff, which could add selling pressure later. Official launch and listing details have been unclear, so double-check contract addresses before using any wallet.

newCoins.name: Doodles
newCoins.what: The Solana token of the Doodles NFT (digital collectible) brand.
newCoins.why: It was among the day's top gainers on several trackers earlier, more than doubling in 24 hours, with no clear project-specific reason reported.
newCoins.redFlags: A tiny market value (tens of millions of dollars) means small trades move the price a lot. No specific catalyst was reported, and spikes like this often reverse within days.
